sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球知名的高等学府，致力于解决食品、能源、健康、教育和环境等全球最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州乃至全球范围内合作创新，寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是该校宗旨的一部分，即提升所有生物的生活质量。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.ucDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 请访问 21stCentury.ucDavis.edu 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》（99% Invisible）。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯（Roman Mars）。

sentences.en: Goethe said that architecture is frozen music.
sentences.zh: 歌德曾说，建筑是凝固的音乐。

sentences.en: That's lovely.
sentences.zh: 这话说得真好。

sentences.en: Of course, that was before audio recording, so now for the most part, music is frozen music.
sentences.zh: 当然，那是录音技术出现之前的事，所以现在对大多数人来说，音乐才是凝固的音乐。

sentences.en: It's only very recently in the history of music that we've been able to freeze music into an object.
sentences.zh: 在音乐史上，我们能够把音乐“冻结”成一件实体物品，其实也就是最近的事。

sentences.en: And in my life, the form of this object mattered a lot.
sentences.zh: 而在我的生活中，这种物品的形态曾占据着非常重要的地位。

sentences.en: I once bought vinyl albums and cassette tapes, and there were two first songs per album.
sentences.zh: 我曾经买过黑胶唱片和磁带，每张专辑都有两首开场曲。

sentences.en: Side A
sentences.zh: A面

sentences.en: And Side B
sentences.zh: 还有B面

sentences.en: The energy of a first song made it stand apart from the other songs.
sentences.zh: 开场曲独有的能量感让它从其他歌曲中脱颖而出。

sentences.en: At least in my head it did.
sentences.zh: 至少在我的脑海里是这样的。

sentences.en: Then the CD came along and eliminated Side B, and there was only one first song.
sentences.zh: 后来CD出现了，它淘汰了B面，只剩下一首开场曲。

sentences.en: And the actual number of the track that you could see prominently displayed on the CD player UI.
sentences.zh: 你可以清晰地看到曲目编号显眼地显示在CD机的屏幕界面上。

sentences.en: That became my index for sorting songs.
sentences.zh: 这就成了我给歌曲归类排序的索引。

sentences.en: Then MP3s jumbled my sense of track order, and albums began to feel more like a loose grouping of individual pieces rather than a conceptual whole.
sentences.zh: 再后来，MP3打乱了我对曲序的概念，专辑开始感觉更像是一堆独立单曲的松散组合，而不是一个概念上的整体。

sentences.en: I could do this all day, and you're welcome to chime in.
sentences.zh: 我一整天都能聊这个，非常欢迎你们随时插话。

sentences.en: Let's totally hash this out on the website.
sentences.zh: 让我们在网站上好好探讨一下吧。

sentences.en: But my point is this.
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是。

sentences.en: When it comes to music, the form of the thing matters.
sentences.zh: 说到音乐，载体的形态至关重要。

sentences.en: But no effect has been as world-changing as the original innovation, freezing music in time onto a recording,
sentences.zh: 但没有任何一种影响能比得上最初的那项创新——将音乐的时间“冻结”在录音中，

sentences.en: where a single version of a song, a single performance of a song, became the song.
sentences.zh: 在这里，一首歌曲的某个单一版本、某次单独的演绎，就成了这首歌本身。

sentences.en: This inherently mutable method of communication was fundamentally changed.
sentences.zh: 这种本质上易变且流动的传播方式被彻底改变了。

sentences.en: Songs are astonishing things, and I also don't think most people really even know what they are.
sentences.zh: 歌曲是奇妙的事物，而且我也觉得大多数人其实并不真正了解它们到底是什么。

sentences.en: That's the songwriter, composer, and producer John Bryan.
sentences.zh: 说话的是词曲作家、作曲家兼制作人约翰·布莱恩（John Bryan）。

sentences.en: Now, I didn't talk to John Bryan, but I know people who did.
sentences.zh: 当然，我并没有采访过约翰·布莱恩，但我认识采访过他的人。

sentences.en: Jim DeRogatis and Greg Cott are the hosts of a radio program I'm a huge fan of called Sound Opinions.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·德罗加蒂斯（Jim DeRogatis）和格雷格·科特（Greg Kot）是一档我非常喜欢的广播节目的主持人，名叫《音乐观点》（Sound Opinions）。

sentences.en: It's a rock and roll talk show.
sentences.zh: 这是一档摇滚乐脱口秀节目。

sentences.en: And if certain niche-y, snarky corners of the internet have darkened your concept of music journalism,
sentences.zh: 如果你对音乐新闻的印象已经被互联网上某些小众、刻薄的角落所玷污，

sentences.en: well, Sound Opinions is your beacon of light, my friends.
sentences.zh: 那么，《音乐观点》就是照亮你们的明灯，朋友们。

sentences.en: Anyway, John Bryan came to WBEZ in Chicago to talk to Sound Opinions in 2006.
sentences.zh: 总之，约翰·布莱恩在2006年来到芝加哥的WBEZ电台做客《音乐观点》。

sentences.en: And at the time, Bryan had just co-produced Kanye West's album Late Registration,
sentences.zh: 当时，布莱恩刚刚联合制作了坎耶·韦斯特（Kanye West）的专辑《迟到的注册》（Late Registration），

sentences.en: and he was also already well-known as a film composer of a lot of really great movies,
sentences.zh: 而且他作为电影配乐家早已声名远扬，创作过许多非常优秀的电影配乐，

sentences.en: many by Paul Thomas Anderson.
sentences.zh: 其中许多作品都出自保罗·托马斯·安德森（Paul Thomas Anderson）之手。

sentences.en: I heard the show broadcast on WBEZ while I was sitting in my car in a parking lot of a taqueria in Logan Square.
sentences.zh: 我当时坐在洛根广场（Logan Square）一家墨西哥卷饼店的停车场车里，收听着WBEZ广播里的这档节目。

sentences.en: And I've thought about this section of their interview about songs versus performances
sentences.zh: 从那以后，至少每个月我都会想起他们采访中关于“歌曲与演绎”的那段讨论，

sentences.en: at least once a month since then.
sentences.zh: 已经六年了。

sentences.en: For six years.
sentences.zh: 整整六年。

sentences.en: But only recently did it dawn on me that this is a perfect 99% Invisible story.
sentences.zh: 但直到最近我才突然意识到，这简直是一个完美的《99%隐形》风格的故事。

sentences.en: So here it is.
sentences.zh: 所以，它来了。

sentences.en: John Bryan on Sound Opinions in 2006.
sentences.zh: 2006年约翰·布莱恩做客《音乐观点》的录音。

sentences.en: I distinguish between, for lack of better terms, I call songs and performance pieces.
sentences.zh: 我做了一个区分，由于找不到更好的词，我称它们为“歌曲”和“演绎作品”。

sentences.en: And what most people like are specific performances.
sentences.zh: 而大多数人喜欢的其实是具体的某一次演绎。

sentences.en: We've grown up in an era of recording.
sentences.zh: 我们是在录音时代长大的一代。

sentences.en: And, you know, the very thing, one of the very things I love, recording has killed people's ability to hear songs
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我深爱的一点——录音技术恰恰扼杀了人们单纯去聆听歌曲本身的能力，

sentences.en: purely as chord change, melody, and lyric.
sentences.zh: 也就是把歌曲纯粹听作和弦走向、旋律和歌词的能力。

sentences.en: It's a very strange and beautiful art form because when it's right, boy, do you know it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常奇妙且美丽的艺术形式，因为当它对味的时候，天哪，你一眼就能听出来。

sentences.en: But what we have sort of lost is, I don't know, the best example I could probably give would be Led Zeppelin.
sentences.zh: 但我们某种程度上丢失的是——我不知道，我能举出的最好例子大概就是齐柏林飞艇乐队（Led Zeppelin）。

sentences.en: Those things are the ultimate performance pieces, and I'm a big fan.
sentences.zh: 那些作品是终极的演绎作品，而我是他们的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: I think they're just absolutely astonishing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们简直叹为观止。

sentences.en: And the sort of dynamics they had are sorely lacking in music today.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有的那种音乐张力和动感，在今天的音乐中已经荡然无存。

sentences.en: Record making is great.
sentences.zh: 制作唱片固然伟大。

sentences.en: A true band in the sense that you really could tell who the individuals were.
sentences.zh: 那是一支真正的乐队，那种你真的能听出每个人独特个性的乐队。

sentences.en: Remarkable thing.
sentences.zh: 了不起的事物。

sentences.en: And I don't consider most of those things songs.
sentences.zh: 而且我并不认为其中大多数东西是真正的歌曲。

sentences.en: And the way I can sort of prove my point is, have you ever listened to anybody else play a Led Zeppelin song
sentences.zh: 我能证明自己观点的方式是，你有没有听过其他人演奏齐柏林飞艇的歌，

sentences.en: and gone, oh, that was a great, satisfying experience?
sentences.zh: 然后感叹：哦，那是一次伟大而过瘾的体验？

sentences.en: Except for Dred Zeppelin, who I loved.
sentences.zh: 除了“钻孔齐柏林”（Dred Zeppelin）乐队之外，我挺喜欢他们的。

sentences.en: What people like is that specific guitar sound, that specific performance in concert with that specific drum sound,
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢的是那种特定的吉他音色、在演唱会上与那种特定鼓声相配合的特定演绎，

sentences.en: with that specific drummer playing that specific part.
sentences.zh: 以及由特定鼓手演奏的特定乐段。

sentences.en: And it's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 这很美妙。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件美好的事情。

sentences.en: There are all different types of art and creative expression.
sentences.zh: 艺术和创意表达的形式千差万别。

sentences.en: However, if I were to sit and go here over on the piano and go,
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我坐到钢琴前弹奏，然后说：

sentences.en: this is the melody to a Led Zeppelin song.
sentences.zh: 这就是齐柏林飞艇某首歌曲的旋律。

sentences.en: And I could play 30 others.
sentences.zh: 我还能弹另外30首。

sentences.en: That's the thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: You know, I know it could sound like a snobbishness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这听起来可能有点装腔作势。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 其实并不是。

sentences.en: I'm telling you, I love these records.
sentences.zh: 我向你保证，我很爱这些唱片。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: They're great.
sentences.zh: 它们棒极了。

sentences.en: However, there's a difference between that and a song, say a Gershwin song,
sentences.zh: 然而，这与一首真正的歌曲之间是有区别的，比如说格什温（Gershwin）的歌，

sentences.en: you could actually play in the style of Led Zeppelin and have a completely satisfying experience.
sentences.zh: 你可以完全用齐柏林飞艇的风格去演奏它，并且获得完全过瘾的音乐体验。

sentences.en: I do it all the time.
sentences.zh: 我经常这么做。

sentences.en: I want to hear that.
sentences.zh: 我很想听听看。

sentences.en: But when you start playing Zeppelin songs, say in the style of like 1920s music,
sentences.zh: 但当你开始用比如20世纪20年代音乐的风格去演奏齐柏林飞艇的歌时，

sentences.en: suddenly it's laid bare that it's like, oh no, it was about those people.
sentences.zh: 突然之间一切就被赤裸裸地揭示出来：哦，原来关键在于那些人本身。

sentences.en: And those people were in a room and it was, and it was great.
sentences.zh: 是那些人聚在一个房间里，然后碰撞出了伟大的火花。

sentences.en: And I love it.
sentences.zh: 我爱极了这种感觉。

sentences.en: But I consider it a performance piece.
sentences.zh: 但我认为那是一部演绎作品。

sentences.en: And I consider a lot of rock that people listen to be performance pieces.
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们听的大多数摇滚乐都是演绎作品。

sentences.en: They're not necessarily songs.
sentences.zh: 它们未必是真正意义上的歌曲。

sentences.en: So, you know, I heard you had Tom York here recently, and there's a guy who's a songwriter.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我听说你们最近请到了汤姆·约克（Thom Yorke），那才是个名副其实的词曲作家。

sentences.en: Comes into the band and goes, here's the thing I've got.
sentences.zh: 他走进排练室对乐队说，这是我写的东西。

sentences.en: And then they, you know, rock with holy hardness and all the greatness they've got with them getting in a room.
sentences.zh: 然后他们，你知道的，带着神圣的坚定和他们聚在一起时所拥有的全部才华，尽情摇滚。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, that's part of what makes a band like Radiohead stand out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，这也是电台司令（Radiohead）这样的乐队能够脱颖而出的原因之一。

sentences.en: You know, when that second record came out, we all collectively went, oh my God, somebody who actually has songs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当他们的第二张专辑问世时，我们所有人都集体感叹：天哪，终于有人写出真正的歌了。

sentences.en: And this guy's an amazing singer.
sentences.zh: 这家伙还是个了不起的歌手。

sentences.en: It isn't extinct yet.
sentences.zh: 这种才华还没绝迹呢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or Cobain, right?
sentences.zh: 或者像科本（Cobain），对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I mean, okay, here, let's do a little musicology course.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，好吧，来，让我们上一堂小型音乐学课。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: If you just go, yeah, it was cool.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是轻描淡写地说，哦，挺酷的。

sentences.en: It was, you know, punk rock.
sentences.zh: 那，你知道，就是朋克摇滚。

sentences.en: It was popular.
sentences.zh: 它很受欢迎。

sentences.en: He had it factor for days.
sentences.zh: 他浑身散发着无与伦比的巨星魅力。

sentences.en: But if you take the average punk rock song, it is that same Led Zeppelin melody, even though they hated Zeppelin so much.
sentences.zh: 但如果你拿出一首普通的朋克摇滚歌曲，你会发现它用的其实就是齐柏林飞艇那种旋律，尽管他们嘴上那么痛恨齐柏林飞艇。

sentences.en: It's pretty funny.
sentences.zh: 这挺搞笑的。

sentences.en: You know, but if it's like, you know, one of a thousand punk songs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，但这就像是成千上万首朋克歌曲中的一首而已。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: There's a big difference between that and, I mean, I can sit here on grand piano, play an unaffected version, and we can all go, oh my God, yeah, that's the best thing ever.
sentences.zh: 这与——我的意思是，我可以坐在三角钢琴前，弹奏一曲未经修饰的原版，然后我们大家都会惊叹：天哪，这简直是史上最棒的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: My spine tingles any time I play that melody over those chord changes.
sentences.zh: 每当我用那些和弦走向弹奏那个旋律时，我的脊椎都会感到一阵酥麻。

sentences.en: Like, that to me, lithium is no different.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这种感觉就像锂元素（Lithium）一样无可替代。

sentences.en: It's in the same realm as being able to go, you know, where, you know, probably like most people, I remember exactly where I was first time I heard lithium.
sentences.zh: 这就好比——可能和大多数人一样，我记得自己第一次听到《Lithium》时确切身处何地。

sentences.en: I remember the back of the friend's car, and it came on, and I just freaked out.
sentences.zh: 我记得是在朋友汽车的后座上，音乐响起来的那一刻，我简直要抓狂了。

sentences.en: I mean, I was nearly in tears.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我当时感动得几乎要流泪。

sentences.en: I'm like, oh my God, that guy's better than everybody's life.
sentences.zh: 我在心里想：天哪，这家伙比世上所有人的生命都要美好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, you know, it was so palpable, like, that's one of the best chord changes I've ever heard.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，那种冲击力是如此触手可及，那是我听过的最好的和弦走向之一。

sentences.en: It's absolutely as good as, you know, Gershwin or Thelonious Monk or any great thing that's existed.
sentences.zh: 它绝对和格什温、塞洛尼斯·孟克（Thelonious Monk）或以往任何伟大的作品不相上下。

sentences.en: That was John Bryan, talking with Jim DeRogatis and Greg Cott on Sound Opinions in 2006.
sentences.zh: 刚才那是约翰·布莱恩于2006年在《音乐观点》节目中与吉姆·德罗加蒂斯和格雷格·科特的对话。

sentences.en: Sound Opinions is produced by WBEZ Chicago and distributed by PRX, the public radio exchange.
sentences.zh: 《音乐观点》由芝加哥WBEZ电台制作，并由公共广播交换平台PRX发行。

sentences.en: Find out more at soundopinions.org.
sentences.zh: 请访问 soundopinions.org 了解更多详情。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week, pretty much by Sound Opinions.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》基本上是由《音乐观点》栏目组制作的。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Robin Lim and Jason Saldana.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢罗宾·林（Robin Lim）和杰森·萨尔达尼亚（Jason Saldana）。

sentences.en: We are a project of KALW 91.7 Local Public Radio in San Francisco and the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山本地公共电台KALW 91.7频道以及旧金山美国建筑师学会（American Institute of Architects）的一个合作项目。

sentences.en: Support for 99% Invisible is provided in part by the Facebook design team, who believes that design can bring positive change to the world.
sentences.zh: 《99%隐形》的部分资金支持来自Facebook设计团队，他们坚信设计能够为世界带来积极的改变。

sentences.en: Visit them at facebook.com slash design.
sentences.zh: 欢迎访问 facebook.com/design 了解他们。

sentences.en: And by tiny letter, email for people with something to say.
sentences.zh: 以及 TinyLetter，专为有话要说的人打造的电子邮件服务。

sentences.en: My boy Carver always has something to say.
sentences.zh: 我的儿子卡弗（Carver）总是有话要说。

sentences.en: What do you have to say, Carver?
sentences.zh: 卡弗，你有什么想说的？

sentences.en: I think that my dad is the beSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我爸爸是最棒的。

sentences.en: But you know, like, if I put that on, everyone's going to say,
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，如果我把这段放出来，每个人都会说：

sentences.en: Oh, Roman, you just made your son say that he's the best, that you're the beSt.
sentences.zh: 哦，罗曼，你分明是让你儿子说他自己是最棒的，也就是你最棒。

sentences.en: What do you have to say about that?
sentences.zh: 对此你有什么想说的吗？

sentences.en: Can I tell you the best about how it all is formed?
sentences.zh: 我能说说这一切是如何形成的吗？

sentences.en: It's the simplest way to write an email newsletter.
sentences.zh: 这是编写电子邮件简报最简单的方式。

sentences.en: tinyletter.com
sentences.zh: tinyletter.com

sentences.en: From the people behind MailChimp.
sentences.zh: 由 MailChimp 幕后的团队倾力打造。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到本节目并给它点赞。

sentences.en: I tweet at Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我的推特账号是 Roman Mars。

sentences.en: And I'm serious.
sentences.zh: 我是认真的。

sentences.en: Let's talk about how the objects of music change the way you both make and listen to music.
sentences.zh: 让我们来聊聊音乐的载体是如何改变你创作和聆听音乐的方式的。

sentences.en: I'm ready to throw down at 99%invisible.org.
sentences.zh: 我已经准备好在 99%invisible.org 上大干一场了。
